verdict.outcome_basis: readout: "True terminate the Phase 3 trial of the investigational medicine evacetrapib, due to insufficient efficacy" (announcement:accelerate)
verdict.consistency: consistent with the calculator (probability of success 14%)

report.headline: The ACCELERATE trial of evacetrapib was stopped for futility in ~12,092 high-risk vascular patients, confirming that CETP inhibition does not reduce cardiovascular events despite large HDL-C increases.
report.summary: ACCELERATE randomized 12,092 patients with high-risk vascular disease to evacetrapib 130 mg or placebo on background statin therapy. The trial was stopped early on October 12, 2015, after a planned interim analysis showed a low probability of achieving the primary composite endpoint (CV death, MI, stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina). No safety signal was identified. The failure aligns with the calculator's prediction of only a 14% probability of success (expected HR 0.958) driven by modest LDL-C lowering (~15% placebo-adjusted in phase 2), while the large HDL-C elevation (54–129% in phase 3, 103% placebo-adjusted in phase 2) is not causal for CVD reduction. Mendelian randomization and prior CETP inhibitor failures (torcetrapib, dalcetrapib) support that HDL-C is a non-causal biomarker. The trial was also underpowered for the small expected effect (MDE HR 0.872 for 80% power vs. expected HR 0.958).
key_evidence: 12,092 participants randomized (Lilly to Discontinue Development of Evacetrapib for High-Risk Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease (Oct 12, 2015); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01687998 ACCELERATE; Assessment of the clinical effects of cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibition with evacetrapib in patients at high-risk for vascular outcomes: Rationale and design of the ACCELERATE trial.)

1,670 planned primary endpoint events (Assessment of the clinical effects of cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibition with evacetrapib in patients at high-risk for vascular outcomes: Rationale and design of the ACCELERATE trial.)

Primary endpoint: composite of CV death, MI, stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina (Assessment of the clinical effects of cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibition with evacetrapib in patients at high-risk for vascular outcomes: Rationale and design of the ACCELERATE trial.; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01687998 ACCELERATE)
Trial stopped early for futility on Oct 12, 2015, with no safety signal (Lilly to Discontinue Development of Evacetrapib for High-Risk Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease (Oct 12, 2015))

Phase 3 HDL-C increase 54–129% at 130 mg (Assessment of the clinical effects of cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibition with evacetrapib in patients at high-risk for vascular outcomes: Rationale and design of the ACCELERATE trial.)

Phase 2 placebo-adjusted HDL-C increase 103% and LDL-C lowering −15% (0.56 mmol/L) at 100 mg + atorvastatin (Efficacy, safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic profile of evacetrapib administered as monotherapy or in combination with atorvastatin in Japanese patients with dyslipidemia.)
Calculator predicted 14% probability of success (expected HR 0.958) based on LDL-C reduction; trial stopped for futility (calculator; verdict)
CETP genetic association score 0.736 but zero genetic evidence items before 2015-10-12 (opentargets:CETP)

No QT prolongation or clinically relevant blood pressure effects at supratherapeutic doses (Effects of the cholesteryl ester transfer protein inhibitor evacetrapib on lipoproteins, apolipoproteins and 24-h ambulatory blood pressure in healthy adults.; Evacetrapib at a supratherapeutic steady state concentration does not prolong QT in a thorough QT/QTc study in healthy participants.)
report.what_would_change_this: A positive result would require evidence that CETP inhibition reduces CVD events through a mechanism other than HDL-C elevation (e.g., larger LDL-C lowering, plaque regression, or anti-inflammatory effects) demonstrated in a trial powered for a realistic effect size. Final ACCELERATE results with observed HR and biomarker changes at 130 mg would settle the quantitative uncertainty.
report.readthrough_note: Other CETP inhibitors have shown mixed results: torcetrapib increased mortality (off-target toxicity), dalcetrapib failed for futility, while anacetrapib showed modest CVD benefit in REVEAL driven by LDL-C lowering. The class effect appears dependent on achieving sufficient LDL-C reduction without off-target harm.

mechanism.target_genetics_rationale: CETP has genetic association score 0.736 for coronary artery disease but all 13 Open Targets studies published after 2015-10-12 cutoff (evidence_before_cutoff: 0). No genetic evidence before cutoff for this well-studied target → uncertain per rules.
mechanism.notes: LDL-C: Used phase 2 combination data (100 mg + atorvastatin 10 mg, 12 wk, placebo-adjusted -15%) as best proxy for phase 3 (130 mg on background statin) despite verifier noting source (pmid:24786356) may describe monotherapy; baseline 144.3 mg/dL converted to 3.731 mmol/L. HDL-C: Corrected per critic — 103% increase at 100 mg + atorvastatin 10 mg is active-comparator adjusted (vs atorvastatin alone), not placebo-adjusted; baseline 55.1 mg/dL. apoB: Used -22.08% at 600 mg Day 14 (placebo-adjusted) from f_2cefec61c26df5; two other verified facts show -19.17% and +80.5% (likely sign error) at same dose/timepoint — discrepancy noted. SBP: 2.88 mmHg rise at supratherapeutic 600 mg Day 14 (placebo-adjusted); no data at 130 mg therapeutic dose. Trial stopped early for futility; planned events 1670 used as actual events not in verified facts.

for.text: The intended biomarker was HDL-C (per calculator inputs), but Mendelian randomization and prior CETP inhibitor failures (torcetrapib, dalcetrapib) show HDL-C elevation is not causal for CVD reduction. The calculator's expected HR of 0.958 is driven almost entirely by the modest LDL-C lowering (-15% in phase 2), not the 103% HDL-C rise.

Phase 3 data at the actual 130 mg dose show HDL-C increases of 54-129% (f_02746d884f6ab5, f_fde73e34804c2b) but LDL-C lowering of only -14% to -36% (f_342c58c5ac1a94, f_fdb5153ab0027b), confirming the drug's primary biomarker effect (HDL-C) is large but non-causal, while the causal biomarker (LDL-C) moves modestly.

against.text: CETP genetic association score is 0.736 with 13 evidence items (f_ff8d155f87441a), suggesting some target-level support, though evidence_before_cutoff=0 indicates limited human genetics evidence available at trial launch.

hypotheses.would_settle: Mendelian randomization studies of CETP variants on CVD outcomes; final ACCELERATE results with observed HR.

for.text: CETP genetic association score 0.736 but evidence_before_cutoff=0 (f_ff8d155f87441a), meaning human genetics did not strongly support CETP inhibition for CVD prevention at the time of trial initiation. The calculator flags 'target genetics: uncertain' as weakest link.

against.text: CETP variants robustly associate with HDL-C levels; the failure may be specific to HDL-C as a mediator rather than the target itself. Other CETP inhibitors (anacetrapib) later showed modest benefit in REVEAL, suggesting the target can work with sufficient LDL-C lowering.

hypotheses.would_settle: Large-scale genetic studies of CETP loss-of-function variants on CVD outcomes; REVEAL trial results (anacetrapib).

for.text: Calculator shows expected HR 0.958 (4.2% RRR) with only 14% power to detect it (MDE HR 0.872 for 80% power). Even using phase 3 LDL-C lowering of -36% (f_fdb5153ab0027b), the expected HR would be ~0.90 with 1.5-year follow-up, still below the 0.872 MDE.

Phase 3 dose (130 mg) produced only -14% LDL-C lowering in one analysis (f_342c58c5ac1a94), which would yield an even smaller expected benefit. The trial was sized for a larger effect than the mechanism delivers at the tested dose.

against.text: If the -36% LDL-C lowering (f_fdb5153ab0027b) is the true effect, the expected HR approaches the MDE threshold, but the trial was stopped early before reaching planned events.

hypotheses.would_settle: Final LDL-C lowering at 130 mg in ACCELERATE; observed HR if trial continued to planned events.

for.text: Phase 2 data at supratherapeutic 600 mg show SBP increase of 2.88 mmHg (f_30b41d9e4ecc71) and 1.69 mmHg (f_73f043d9486743), which the calculator incorporates as a BP factor of 1.038 (HR penalty).

against.text: Phase 2 assessment at 600 mg explicitly states 'Evacetrapib was devoid of clinically relevant effects on blood pressure and mineralocorticoid levels' (f_94aa24404d8460). No safety signal in ACCELERATE itself (f_c6022efac3361f: False). The SBP effect at therapeutic 130 mg is unknown but likely smaller.

hypotheses.would_settle: SBP change at 130 mg in phase 3; final safety data from ACCELERATE.

for.text: Median follow-up of 1.5 years (f_13d6532df5671c) may be insufficient for atherosclerosis regression benefits to fully manifest. Composite endpoint includes coronary revascularization and hospitalization for unstable angina, which are softer components.

against.text: Standard CVOT design with 1670 planned events (f_7262d7298b3588) and 1.5-year follow-up is typical for high-risk secondary prevention. The trial was stopped for futility, not because of design flaws per se.

hypotheses.would_settle: Longer-term follow-up data; comparison with trials using harder endpoints (e.g., 3-point MACE).

for.text: Trial stopped early for futility based on periodic data reviews showing 'low probability the study would achieve its primary endpoint' (f_167ee16f8aa344, f_8b5fdcfca5f27e). This is a scientific (statistical) decision, not a business decision.

against.text: Early stopping for futility is a pre-specified, scientifically valid execution decision. It does not indicate poor adherence, recruitment failure, or sponsor withdrawal for non-scientific reasons.

hypotheses.would_settle: Independent statistical analysis of the interim data that triggered futility stopping.

for.text: High-risk vascular disease patients on background statin therapy (per inclusion criteria f_00271dd86d1d7d, f_7ea8865ee8486e) may have event rates driven by non-atherosclerotic processes (e.g., heart failure, arrhythmia) that CETP inhibition does not address.

against.text: Primary endpoint components (CV death, MI, stroke, coronary revascularization, UA hospitalization) are predominantly atherosclerotic. The population is the standard secondary prevention population for lipid-lowering trials.

hypotheses.would_settle: Cause-specific event breakdown in ACCELERATE; subgroup analyses by baseline risk factors.

for.text: As of 2015-10-12 (as_of date), the trial was stopped early and final results (observed HR, CI) were not yet available (calculator shows observed_hr: null, observed_ci: null). The calculator's expected HR is based on phase 2 biomarker data at non-therapeutic doses (100 mg + atorvastatin for LDL-C/HDL-C, 600 mg for apoB/SBP) rather than phase 3 data at 130 mg.

Key discrepancies: LDL-C input uses phase 2 combination therapy data (-15% at 100 mg + atorvastatin) but phase 3 used 130 mg monotherapy on background statin with -14% to -36% LDL-C lowering. SBP input uses 600 mg supratherapeutic dose. These limit quantitative precision of the expected HR.

against.text: The qualitative conclusion (biomarker_not_causal) is robust to these quantitative uncertainties because HDL-C non-causality is established by genetics and prior CETP failures, and even optimistic phase 3 LDL-C lowering yields an underpowered trial.

hypotheses.would_settle: Publication of final ACCELERATE results with observed HR and biomarker changes at 130 mg.
